# Best Rower for Home Use: 5 Questions That Predict Whether You'll Still Use It in a Year


Last updated November 2026


The best home rower is the one you're happy to sit back down on tomorrow.


**Short answer:** For most homes, the best rower is the Aviron Strong Series. Garage Gym Reviews, whose trainers have tested more than 30 rowing machines, names it the Best Overall High-End Rowing Machine, and BarBend picks it as the Best Magnetic Rowing Machine. It stores upright, runs at about 60 decibels, fits rowers up to 6'8" and 507 lb, and comes with 1,000+ workouts. Specs only get you so far, though. Five questions predict whether any home rower still gets used a year from now.


Plenty of rowers row well. At home, the harder test is whether you're still using one after the box goes out with the recycling. Most home equipment hits the motivation cliff around month two and spends the next few years as an expensive clothes rack. Below are the picks from two independent testing sites, then five questions about how a rower fits into a real house and a real schedule.

Our guide to the[best rowing machine for home](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/best-rowing-machine-for-home/) compares fit, games and noise across four brands.

Both sites scored durability and programming 5 out of 5. A solid frame keeps a rower running for years, and the programming decides whether you want to get on it.


## 1. Will It Fit Your Body and Your Room?


A rower that's cramped for your legs, or too long for the spare room, never turns into a habit. Check three numbers first:


- **Your height and weight.** The Strong Series holds up to 507 lb and fits rowers up to 6'8".
- **The floor it needs.** It's 84 inches (7 feet) long and 27 inches wide. BarBend says the average rower it has tested runs roughly 9 feet.
- **The ceiling it needs.** Stored upright, it takes a 35 x 27 inch patch of floor and stands 83 inches tall, so it clears a standard 8-foot ceiling. It doesn't need a wall mount, and front wheels let you roll it out of the way.


Seat height is easy to overlook. The Strong Series seat sits about 20 inches off the floor, so getting on and off is easier on knees and hips, especially when you're tired after a workout.


"Being 76 with spinal stenosis, the higher seat was a gift. I don't think I would have invested in a rowing machine without that option."


**Sarah Lersch** , Strong Series Rower owner · Verified Buyer


Tipped up on its front wheels, the Strong Series stands on a 35 x 27 inch patch of floor. No wall mount needed.


## 2. Can You Row at 6 a.m. Without Waking the House?


Home workouts happen when the house allows: before the kids are up, after they're down, or while someone's on a call in the next room. How loud a rower is depends mostly on its resistance type:


- **Magnetic** is the quietest. Magnets create the resistance, so you mostly hear the seat rolling.
- **Air** uses a fan, and it gets louder the harder you pull.
- **Water** makes a steady swoosh from the paddles in the tank.


The Strong Series pairs magnetic and air resistance with a nylon belt instead of a chain, and Aviron rates it at about 60 decibels, roughly conversation volume. BarBend does flag the air side, saying it "isn't so loud that it drowns out your programming," and its tester suggests Bluetooth headphones "to fully lock in." For more numbers, see[how loud a rowing machine is](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/how-loud-is-a-rowing-machine/) .


## 3. Will Month Three Feel Different From Week One?


A[2015 systematic review of 24 studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25921307/) in the *Annals of Behavioral Medicine* found that how good exercise felt during a moderate workout was linked to how much people exercised later. How they felt afterward wasn't. For a rower, that means the workout itself has to be something you enjoy while you're doing it.


A screen with nothing new on it fails that test. By week six you know every split by heart. The Strong Series comes with 1,000+ workouts across science-backed games, coached classes, scenic rows and live races, plus streaming apps like Netflix, YouTube and Disney+ for easy days, so Tuesday doesn't have to look like Monday. Garage Gym Reviews rated the programming 5 out of 5, and so did BarBend's rowing tester.


"I have never been the kind of person to stick to working out well. I fall off the horse constantly. But with Aviron on days I just want to YouTube binge, I do that while rowing. When I have the energy for high intensity there's workouts for that. If I'm feeling competitive, I can do that."


**Jorge Zuniga** , Aviron owner · Verified Buyer

## When Is a Different Rower the Better Pick?


A different rower makes more sense in a few cases:


- **You want the lowest price and don't need a screen.** A basic air or magnetic rower costs less. Just plan your own way to keep it interesting past month two.
- **You train for indoor rowing races or CrossFit.** The Concept2 RowErg is the standard in those gyms and needs no subscription.
- **You have a very long stroke.** Garage Gym Reviews notes the Strong Series' shorter length "may feel constricting for some." If that's you, test it during the trial.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What type of rowing machine is best for home use?


For most homes, a magnetic or magnetic-plus-air rower. Magnetic resistance is the quietest, and air adds a feel that ramps up with effort. Water rowers have a lovely sound but carry a tank of water, which makes them heavier to move. If floor space is tight, pick one that stores upright.


### How much space do you need for a rowing machine at home?


Plan for the machine's length plus room to step on and off beside it. The Strong Series is 84 inches long and 27 inches wide in use, and 35 x 27 inches on the floor when stored upright, at 83 inches tall. BarBend says the average rower it has tested is about 9 feet long, so check the length of anything you're comparing.


### Can you use an Aviron rower without a membership?


Yes. The membership is recommended but not required. Without it you can track live metrics, create profiles, follow friends, see your workout history and adjust resistance. The games, coached classes, scenic rows and live races come with the membership, which covers the whole family.


### Is a rower or a bike better for a home gym?


A rower works your legs, core, back and arms in every stroke. A bike mostly works your legs and takes up less floor. If you only have room for one machine and want a full-body workout, the rower covers more. Our[rowing machine vs exercise bike](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/rowing-machine-vs-exercise-bike/) guide goes deeper.


### Is it worth buying a rowing machine for home?


It is if you'll use it. Every $1,000 of rower used three times a week for three years works out to about $2.14 per workout. The same rower used twice costs $500 a session, so how often you'll use it matters more than the price tag.
